title: @streetraceing/package configuration
description: Strict JSON configuration for the @streetraceing/package CLI. Store this object in .packagerc or .packagerc.json.
markdownDescription:
Strict JSON configuration for `@streetraceing/package`. Store the object in `.packagerc` or `.packagerc.json`.

All options have conservative defaults: package and apply hooks are disabled, apply keeps source archives, conflicts abort, symbolic links are not followed, and deleted-file caching is enabled so destructive CLI operations remain recoverable.

$schema.description: Enables editor completion and validation for .packagerc.
$schema.markdownDescription:
Connects `.packagerc` to the published JSON Schema so supported editors can provide validation, hover documentation, and completion.

Keep the value exactly as shown.

type.markdownDescription:
Selects the output archive format.

`zip` - Create a standard ZIP archive. This is currently the only supported format.

root.description: Project root resolved from the directory where the CLI is started.
root.markdownDescription:
Project directory used as the working root for collection, hooks, archive naming, and apply operations.

`.` - Use the current project directory.

`./packages/app` - Package a nested project.

output.description: Output directory resolved relative to the project root.
output.markdownDescription:
Directory where generated archives are written. Relative values are resolved from `root`.

`.` - Write beside the project files.

`./artifacts` - Write into an artifacts directory.

name.markdownDescription:
Filename used by `package zip` when `--output` is omitted.

`{folder}` - Replaced with the project root folder name.

`{workspace}` and `{workspaces}` - Replaced with a filesystem-safe workspace label when scoped monorepo packaging is active. With the default `{folder}.zip`, a single selected workspace automatically uses `<workspace>.zip`.

strategy.markdownDescription:
`git` - Prefer `git ls-files` so nested `.gitignore`, repository excludes, tracked files, and untracked non-ignored files follow Git behavior. Falls back to the internal walker when Git is unavailable.

`walk` - Always use the built-in filesystem walker and ignore matcher.

gitignore.markdownDescription:
`true` - Apply `.gitignore` and standard Git exclusions.

`false` - Do not use `.gitignore` rules. Reserved package metadata and internal exclusions still apply.

npmignore.description: Legacy alias for packageManagerIgnore when using .npmignore.
npmignore.markdownDescription:
Backward-compatible alias for `packageManagerIgnore`. New configuration should use `packageManagerIgnore` and `packageManagerIgnoreFile`.

`true` - Apply the configured package-manager ignore file.

`false` - Do not enable that filter through this legacy option.

packageManager.description: Package-manager or build-runner command exposed to lifecycle hooks.
packageManager.markdownDescription:
Command used by the `{packageManager}` hook placeholder and exposed as `PACKAGE_MANAGER`. It defaults to `npm`, but may be `pnpm`, `yarn`, `bun`, or any executable command accepted by the shell.

Package never rewrites explicit hook commands; use `{packageManager}` where the configured command should be substituted.

packageManagerIgnore.description: Apply the configured package-manager ignore file during collection.
packageManagerIgnore.markdownDescription:
`true` - Exclude paths matched by `packageManagerIgnoreFile` in addition to other filters.

`false` - Do not read that file. `npmignore` remains a backward-compatible alias.

packageManagerIgnoreFile.description: Ignore-file name used when packageManagerIgnore is enabled.
packageManagerIgnoreFile.markdownDescription:
The ignore filename read in each traversed directory when `packageManagerIgnore` is `true`. The npm-compatible default is `.npmignore`; set another filename for a different build system or package manager.

Examples: `.npmignore`, `.publishignore`, `.releaseignore`.

include.description: Glob patterns selecting files eligible for packaging.
include.markdownDescription:
Ordered allow-list of project-relative glob patterns. A file must match at least one entry before ignore rules are applied.

`**/*` - Select every regular file recursively.

`src/**` - Select only files below `src`.

ignore.description: Additional project-relative glob patterns to exclude.
ignore.markdownDescription:
Extra deny-list evaluated after standard exclusions. Empty by default, so enabling the option does not remove additional files.

`dist/**` - Exclude generated output.

`src/assets/**` - Exclude a subtree.

forceInclude.description: Glob patterns that include files despite normal selection and ignore rules.
forceInclude.markdownDescription:
Paths matching these project-relative globs are included even when excluded by `include`, `ignore`, dotfile filtering, `.gitignore`, or the configured package-manager ignore file.

Safety exclusions still win: `.git`, `node_modules`, reserved Package metadata, and the archive currently being written are never collected. `forceIgnore` has higher priority than `forceInclude`.

forceIgnore.description: Glob patterns that exclude files despite normal include or forceInclude rules.
forceIgnore.markdownDescription:
Highest-priority user-defined deny-list. Paths matching these project-relative globs are excluded even when `forceInclude`, `include`, or ignore-file negation would otherwise select them.

Safety exclusions remain enforced independently.

dot.description: Include dotfiles unless another rule excludes them.
dot.markdownDescription:
`true` - Allow files such as `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `.npmrc`.

`false` - Exclude ordinary dotfiles. Reserved `.packagemanifest.json` and `.packageshift` handling is independent.

followSymlinks.description: Follow symbolic links while walking the project.
followSymlinks.markdownDescription:
`false` - Do not follow symbolic links. This is the safe default and prevents collecting content outside the project root.

`true` - Follow links only when the resolved target remains inside `root`.

includeEmptyDirectories.markdownDescription:
`false` - Store files only, preserving existing archive behavior.

`true` - Add entries for selected empty directories when supported by collection.

manifest.markdownDescription:
`true` - Write `.packagemanifest.json` with file size, mode, SHA-256, and root hash metadata.

`false` - Reserved for manifestless workflows. Disabling metadata reduces base verification and is not recommended.

shiftFile.description: Project-relative source file embedded as .packageshift when present.
shiftFile.markdownDescription:
Path to the source `.packageshift` file. `package zip` validates it and stores it under the reserved archive path `.packageshift`, regardless of dotfile, include, ignore, or Git filtering.

The protocol header inside the file remains `PACKAGESHIFT 1`.

compressionLevel.markdownDescription:
`0` - Store entries without deflate compression.

`1` - Faster compression with larger output.

`9` - Maximum compression and the default.

deterministic.description: Normalize archive metadata for reproducible output.
deterministic.markdownDescription:
`true` - Sort entries and normalize timestamps so unchanged inputs produce stable archives.

`false` - Allow source metadata to influence archive bytes.

preserveMode.markdownDescription:
`true` - Record source permission modes in manifest and ZIP metadata.

`false` - Normalize file modes to `0644`.

preserveMtime.markdownDescription:
`false` - Omit source mtimes from the manifest and use deterministic ZIP timestamps.

`true` - Store source mtimes; this can make otherwise identical archives differ.

sensitiveFiles.description: Behavior when selected paths look sensitive.
sensitiveFiles.markdownDescription:
`warn` - Package files but print a warning. This preserves usability without silently discarding files.

`error` - Stop packaging before the archive is written.

`allow` - Package without a sensitive-file warning.

backupOnApply.description: Create a persistent rollback archive before apply.
backupOnApply.markdownDescription:
`true` - Before a successful `apply` writes project files, save every affected path as a versioned rollback archive under the current user's package data directory. The default location is `~/streetraceing/.package/backups/<project-id>` on Linux and macOS and `%USERPROFILE%\streetraceing\.package\backups\<project-id>` on Windows. Use `package backup list`, `package backup inspect <version>`, and `package backup restore <version>` to work with history.

`false` - Do not create a persistent version. In-memory rollback is still attempted when the current apply operation fails.

conflictStrategy.description: Default apply behavior for local and hash conflicts.
conflictStrategy.markdownDescription:
`abort` - Make no changes when an unresolved conflict exists. This is the safe default.

`overwrite` - Replace conflicting local paths.

`skip` - Keep conflicting local paths and apply non-conflicting changes.

renameDetection.description: Detect exact renames while creating shift archives.
renameDetection.markdownDescription:
`true` - Pair removed and added files with identical SHA-256 content and emit `MOVE` instructions in `.packageshift`.

`false` - Represent the same change as a removal plus payload addition.

renameThreshold.description: Similarity threshold reserved for approximate rename detection.
renameThreshold.markdownDescription:
A number from `0` to `1`.

`0.8` - Require 80% similarity when approximate rename detection becomes available. Exact hash-based detection is used today.

beforePackage.description: Shell commands executed before creating a snapshot or shift archive.
beforePackage.markdownDescription:
Commands run sequentially from the owning project's `root` before file collection for `package zip` and `package shift`. An empty array preserves current behavior. A non-zero exit stops packaging before a new archive is written.

`"npm run build"` - Run one command.

`["npm run lint", "npm run build"]` - Run multiple commands in order.

Available environment variables:

`PACKAGE_HOOK` - `beforePackage`

`PACKAGE_COMMAND` - `zip` or `shift`

`PACKAGE_ROOT` - Absolute project root

`PACKAGE_ARCHIVE` - Absolute intended archive path

When `depends_on` is used, this hook is loaded from every project's `.packagerc` and runs in that project's own directory in dependency-first order. `PACKAGE_PROJECT_NAME`, `PACKAGE_PROJECT_PATH`, and `PACKAGE_COMPOSITION_ROOT` identify the active project and shared archive root.

afterPackage.description: Shell commands executed after a snapshot or shift archive is written.
afterPackage.markdownDescription:
Commands run sequentially from the owning project's `root` only after the archive is successfully created. An empty array preserves current behavior. If a command fails, the created archive is retained and the CLI exits with an error.

`"node scripts/report-package.mjs"` - Run one command.

`["npm run checksum", "npm run publish:artifact"]` - Run multiple commands in order.

Available environment variables:

`PACKAGE_HOOK` - `afterPackage`

`PACKAGE_COMMAND` - `zip` or `shift`

`PACKAGE_ROOT` - Absolute project root

`PACKAGE_ARCHIVE` - Absolute created archive path

When `depends_on` is used, this hook is loaded from every project's `.packagerc` and runs in that project's own directory in dependency-first order. `PACKAGE_PROJECT_NAME`, `PACKAGE_PROJECT_PATH`, and `PACKAGE_COMPOSITION_ROOT` identify the active project and shared archive root.

beforeApply.description: Shell commands executed before applying archive changes.
beforeApply.markdownDescription:
Commands run sequentially from the owning project's `root` after archive validation, conflict handling, and user confirmation, but before the first project file is changed. An empty array preserves current behavior. A non-zero exit stops apply before package changes are written. The hook is not run for `--dry-run`.

`"npm run preapply"` - Run one command.

`["npm run validate", "npm run migrate"]` - Run multiple commands in order.

Available environment variables:

`PACKAGE_HOOK` - `beforeApply`

`PACKAGE_COMMAND` - `apply`

`PACKAGE_ROOT` - Absolute target project root

`PACKAGE_ARCHIVE` - Absolute source archive path

When `depends_on` is used, this hook is loaded from every project's `.packagerc` and runs in that project's own directory in dependency-first order. `PACKAGE_PROJECT_NAME`, `PACKAGE_PROJECT_PATH`, and `PACKAGE_COMPOSITION_ROOT` identify the active project and shared archive root.

afterApply.description: Best-effort shell commands executed after archive changes are applied successfully.
afterApply.markdownDescription:
Commands run sequentially from the owning project's `root` only after all package changes are applied successfully. A non-zero exit or start error is reported as a warning: applied files are not rolled back, the CLI remains successful, remaining `afterApply` commands continue, and optional archive cleanup still runs. An empty array preserves current behavior. The hook is not run for `--dry-run`, cancelled apply, validation failure, conflict abort, or rollback.

`"npm run prepare"` - Run one command.

`["npm install", "npm run build"]` - Run multiple commands in order, continuing after individual failures.

Available environment variables:

`PACKAGE_HOOK` - `afterApply`

`PACKAGE_COMMAND` - `apply`

`PACKAGE_ROOT` - Absolute target project root

`PACKAGE_ARCHIVE` - Absolute source archive path

When `depends_on` is used, this hook is loaded from every project's `.packagerc` and runs in that project's own directory in dependency-first order. `PACKAGE_PROJECT_NAME`, `PACKAGE_PROJECT_PATH`, and `PACKAGE_COMPOSITION_ROOT` identify the active project and shared archive root.

deletePackageOnApply.description: Delete the applied archive after a successful apply.
deletePackageOnApply.markdownDescription:
`false` - Keep the archive passed to `package apply`. This is the non-destructive default.

`true` - Delete the applied archive after project files are applied. Best-effort `afterApply` failures are warnings and do not prevent deletion. The archive is retained during `--dry-run`, on validation errors, conflicts, cancellation, or rollback.

`--delete-package` - Enable this behavior for one apply.

`--keep-package` - Disable it for one apply.

deleteSourcePackageOnApply.description: Delete the exact source snapshot after a successful apply.
deleteSourcePackageOnApply.markdownDescription:
`false` - Keep source snapshot archives. This is the non-destructive default and preserves existing behavior.

`true` - After project files are applied and best-effort `afterApply` hooks run, delete one safely identified source snapshot. The CLI first uses the exact name and SHA-256 recorded by `package shift`. If that reference is unavailable, it searches only beside the applied archive and in the target project root for exactly one regular `.zip` snapshot whose embedded manifest matches the project state captured before apply. Ambiguous matches, symlinks, changed archives, missing metadata, dry runs, cancelled applies, validation failures, and rolled-back applies are never deleted.

`--delete-source-package` - Enable this behavior for one apply.

`--keep-source-package` - Disable it for one apply.

saveDeletedCache.description: Save files that the CLI is about to delete or replace in the user cache.
saveDeletedCache.markdownDescription:
`true` - Before Package deletes or replaces a regular file, copy its current contents to the per-project deleted-file cache. The default location is `~/streetraceing/.package/cache/<project-id>/<operation-id>` on Linux and macOS and `%USERPROFILE%\streetraceing\.package\cache\<project-id>\<operation-id>` on Windows. Each operation includes `.packagecache.json` metadata with original paths, reasons, sizes, modes, and SHA-256 values.

Covered operations include project files removed or overwritten by `apply`, files replaced by `backup restore`, existing output archives replaced by `zip` or `shift`, `.packagerc` replaced by `init --force`, and archives removed by `deletePackageOnApply` or `deleteSourcePackageOnApply`. Files deleted by user-defined hook scripts cannot be intercepted.

Files larger than `10 MiB` are still cached, but the CLI prints a warning before continuing. Cache writes are performed before the destructive action; if a required cache write fails, Package does not perform that deletion or replacement.

`false` - Do not create deleted-file cache copies. Versioned apply backups remain controlled separately by `backupOnApply`.

`--save-deleted-cache` - Enable caching for one command.

`--no-save-deleted-cache` - Disable caching for one command.

depends_on.description: Compose this project with explicitly declared local project dependencies.
depends_on.markdownDescription:
Declares other local projects that must travel with the current project. Paths are resolved from this project's effective `root`. Each dependency loads and applies its own `.packagerc`, may declare further `depends_on` projects, and is stored in the archive under the shared parent directory. Dependency cycles and duplicate project names are rejected. Lifecycle hooks run in each project's own directory in dependency-first order.

`["../backend"]` - Include a sibling project using its package name or folder name.

`[{ "path": "../backend", "name": "@codeissue/backend" }]` - Include a sibling with an explicit stable name.

path.description: Path to the dependent project directory, relative to this project root.

name.description: Optional stable project name. Defaults to package.json name or the directory name.

monorepo.description: Workspace discovery and scoped packaging for monorepositories.
monorepo.markdownDescription: Configures first-class `npm`, `pnpm`, Yarn/Bun, Lerna, and Rush workspace discovery. An empty `selection` preserves whole-repository packaging. Selectors may use a package name, relative workspace path, basename, or glob. Scoped archives keep paths relative to the monorepo root so `diff`, `shift`, and `apply` remain root-safe.

mode.markdownDescription:
`auto` - Enable discovery when workspace metadata exists.

`on` - Also probe common directories such as `packages/*` and `apps/*`.

`off` - Disable workspace selection.

workspacePatterns.markdownDescription: Adds project-relative workspace globs such as `packages/*` or `apps/**`. Prefix a pattern with `!` to exclude matches. These patterns are combined with detected package-manager metadata.

selection.description: Workspace selectors used for scoped collection.
selection.markdownDescription: An empty array packages the whole repository for backward compatibility. Entries match workspace package names, relative paths, basenames, or globs. The CLI `--workspace` and `--all-workspaces` flags override this list.

includeDependencies.description: Expand selection to local workspace dependencies.
includeDependencies.markdownDescription:
`true` - Recursively include selected workspaces' local dependencies from dependency fields.

`false` - Package only directly selected workspaces. Use `--with-dependencies` for one command.

includeDependents.description: Expand selection to local workspace dependents.
includeDependents.markdownDescription:
`true` - Recursively include local workspaces that depend on a selected workspace.

`false` - Do not expand in the reverse direction. Use `--with-dependents` for one command.

includeRootFiles.description: Include configured shared root files in scoped archives.
includeRootFiles.markdownDescription:
`true` - Include paths matched by `monorepo.shared`, such as lockfiles and root build configuration.

`false` - Include only selected workspace trees, except explicit `forceInclude` matches.

shared.description: Root-shared files and globs included with scoped workspaces.
shared.markdownDescription: Project-relative globs for files needed by selected workspaces, including root `package.json`, lockfiles, workspace declarations, TypeScript/build configuration, and Package configuration. Add entries such as `scripts/**` or `.github/**` when those files are required by the scoped archive.
